messages:
Jules K: Hey folks  small weird one. My manager blocked my planned bridge day (Fri after a Thu public holiday) because of a release freeze. I'm 0.75 FTE. Can that bridge day be carried over or converted to pay? cc @People Ops
People Ops: Hi Jules  short answer: bridge days that fall inside mandatory blackout/maintenance windows follow the blackout-exception flow. For part-time staff we pro-rate the entitlement and can either carry the hours forward or do a one-time payout depending on local law and payroll timing.
Jules K: Which form do I use and what's the deadline? Payroll cutoff is coming up for contractor payroll.
People Ops: Use the blackout-exception form: https://intranet.redwood/hr-forms/blackout-exception. Submit within 30 days of the blackout end for standard handling. If you want a payout this pay cycle, note payroll cutoff (see Payroll Bot) and mark the form "payout" + include desired payroll run.
Anya P: I confirm Jules was scheduled on the release crew that week and couldn't take the day. Happy to sign the manager confirmation. :+1:
People Ops: Thanks Anya  we'll open case HR-2026-8011 once submitted. Example proration: 0.75 FTE -> 0.75 of a day; we convert to hours (0.75 * 8 = 6h) and either add to time-off balance or payout equivalent hours. If carryover would breach the 1-day cap, we may convert the excess to payout unless exceptional approval granted.
Payroll Bot: Reminder: payroll cutoff for next cycle is 12 business days before payrun. Payout requests received after that roll to the next cycle.
Jules K: Submitted the form, attached Anya's note and marked "carryover". Marked urgent due to travel plan.
People Ops: Received. We'll validate FTE at blackout date and confirm hours. Expect update in 3	6 business days. If you need payout instead and are inside the cutoff, update the form to "payout" and we'll try to expedite.
calendar-bot: Note: maintenance blackout Nov 22-24. See https://calendar.redwood/blackouts
Jules K: Thanks  appreciate the quick help.
People Ops: You're welcome  we'll update HR-2026-8011 once payroll confirms the pro-rated hours or payout scheduling.
